Key points for the decision:

1. Core premise wrong: Permission Model is not a tenant-isolation boundary. Permissions doc: "This feature does not protect against malicious code. Node.js trusts any code it is asked to run... Malicious code can bypass the permission model and execute arbitrary code without restriction." SECURITY.md threat model: Node trusts the code it runs; code inherits privileges of execution user; also explicit "Permission Model Boundaries" section: designed to reduce blast radius of mistakes in trusted code, not security boundary. So customer-uploaded JS must run in OS-level isolation (containers per tenant, separate users), process._debugProcess caveat: even with no grants, a sandboxed process can force other same-user Node processes to open inspector → need different OS users.

2. Staging/production flags: --permission-audit is audit-only (violations published to diagnostics_channel, no ERR_ACCESS_DENIED, execution continues). Also if both given, --permission takes precedence. Audit mode is fine for discovery in staging; fine as described. Just note it's not enforcement.

3. FS read grant: --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js: wildcard semantics — "After passing a wildcard character (*) all subsequent characters will be ignored. For example: /home/*.js will work similar to /home/*." So the intended ".js only" grant actually allows reading everything under /srv/jobs/, not just .js files. Also directories get wildcard auto-added if the directory exists.

4. --env-file: env files are read before the Permission Model is initialized; such flags "are not subject to the rules of the Permission Model." So loading an env file outside the read list is not blocked — this means the read list is not a complete inventory of what the process reads at startup, and env files (and any V8 flags) sidestep the model. For trusted code this is fine/expected; as an isolation story it breaks the claim that the allowlist bounds reading. Also drop() caveat maybe relevant: dropping doesn't revoke already-open fds.

5. FD: "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model." So passing an already-open fd defeats checks; application must close resources. Use for trusted app code pattern; not fine for untrusted-code boundary.

6. Symlinks: "Symbolic links will be followed even to locations outside the granted paths. Relative symbolic links may allow access to arbitrary files and directories. You must ensure no granted paths contain relative symlinks." Job dirs may contain relative symlinks → assumption must change: sanitize job dirs / forbid symlinks.
